subject: Post-demo: Clarifying throughput, concurrency, and quota for FinLytics
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Clarifying throughput, concurrency, and quota for FinLytics

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and I appreciate the clear product context. Per our demo, I wanted to capture the follow-ups and a few questions so we can size a proposal and request the right quota bump (if Hosted) or scope Dedicated pilot sizing.

Recap / what I captured from the call:
- Primary workload: customer support summarization + retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for a mix of short and long conversations.
- Expected steady state: ~1,800 requests/min across API (mix of chat and streaming).
- Peak windows: 3–5 minute bursts 3x/day, peaks up to ~4,500 requests/min.
- Concurrency need: you mentioned ~1,200 parallel active connections during peak (mostly streaming).
- Streaming: token-by-token streaming required for the front-end UX; low-latency tail important (p95 target ~300ms for small responses, p95 for long-stream end-to-end <1.8s).

Questions / ask from our side:
1) Can you confirm the 1,200 concurrent figure is simultaneous open connections (long-polling/streaming) vs. concurrent in-flight requests number?
2) Typical average request size (tokens in / tokens out) for the RAG flows and average context lengths?
3) Any constraints on connection pooling / keep-alive (e.g., mobile clients vs server-side proxies)?
4) Are there regulatory/audit requirements that affect log retention or access patterns?

Attachments: I can take a more detailed concurrency profile if you can share any telemetry — I attached a simple template (FinLytics-Concurrency-Profile.xlsx) for your convenience.

Next steps I propose:
- You send the completed concurrency profile + any sample traces.
- We run a quick internal sizing review with Platform and Solutions (Neha).
- I’ll open an Ops request for a provisional rate/quota increase for a 30-day pilot while we validate. If the numbers need it, we’ll propose a Dedicated reserved pool for guaranteed concurrency.

Happy to hop on a short technical follow-up with Neha if helpful — she’s looped here.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

--
Attachment: FinLytics-Concurrency-Profile.xlsx (template - please populate)

From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@finlytics.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clarifying throughput, concurrency, and quota for FinLytics

Alex —

Thanks for the clear recap and the template. Quick answers below and I attached our telemetry export.

- Confirming: the ~1,200 number is simultaneous open streaming connections (most are web socket/HTTP2 streams from our web clients).
- Average request: ~40 tokens in, ~120 tokens out for short chats; for RAG flows it varies but average context window ~1,500 tokens and generated length ~350 tokens.
- Peaks: during our billing alerts we see bursts up to ~4,500 requests/min for short bursts (1–4 minutes).
- Connection pooling: we terminate on NGINX proxies in front of our app — keep-alive is enabled with pooled upstreams; we do see idle timeouts at ~60s.
- Compliance: we need 12 months of request metadata for audit (no full PII), and ability to export request IDs for customer records.

Attached: FinLytics-Concurrency-Profile.xlsx (filled)

We’re open to a 30-day pilot. Prefer Hosted if the quota can support streaming latency and concurrent connections; otherwise tell us your recommended Dedicated sizing + cost.

—Sarah
Sarah Connors
Head of Platform Engineering, FinLytics
sarah.connors@finlytics.com | +1 (617) 555-4390

--
Attachment: FinLytics-Concurrency-Profile.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: Clarifying throughput, concurrency, and quota for FinLytics

Internal notes — forwarding Sarah's filled profile. Key points for sizing:
- 1,200 sustained concurrent streaming connections is higher than default Hosted limits.
- Bursty peaks to 4.5k RPM mean we need headroom on token throughput and connection slots.
- Audit retention asks are standard; Storage/egress needs minimal but we should confirm export APIs.

Options to propose to customer:
1) Hosted with provisional quota bump: grant elevated concurrent connection quota to 3,500 and burstable throughput to 4,800 RPM for a 30-day pilot while we validate tail latency and costs. Sales Ops to scope billing/credit.
2) Dedicated pilot: recommend a 2x reserved GPU pool with autoscale headroom; provides guaranteed connection slots and predictable unit cost.

Actions for this thread:
- Rishi: can you open an Ops ticket to evaluate safety of a temporary Hosted quota increase (include redwood-rate-limits-summary.pdf)?
- Neha: please prepare a 45-min technical deep-dive to validate streaming tail latency and keep-alive behavior with their NGINX front-end.
- Alex: propose the pilot dates and draft SOW / MOU for 30-day pilot.

I attached the rate limits summary to help Ops.

-Marissa
VP, Solutions & GTM | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

--
Attachment: redwood-rate-limits-summary.pdf

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@finlytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Clarifying throughput, concurrency, and quota for FinLytics

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the detail and the completed profile. Based on the numbers you provided and internal review, here’s what we can propose as an initial, practical path forward:

Proposed pilot (30 days):
- Elevated Hosted quota: 3,500 concurrent streaming connections (soft limit) with automated burst handling to 5,000 req/min for short windows.
- Sustained throughput target we’ll instrument for: 2,000 req/min with autoscaling backstop.
- Streaming support: full token-by-token streaming with p95 tail SLO target of <1.0s for small responses and <1.8s for long RAG responses during pilot.
- Audit/export: we’ll enable request metadata retention for 12 months and provide an export path for request IDs.

Contingencies / next steps:
1) Sales Ops will open the provisional quota request if you confirm you want to run the pilot (I’ll copy you on that ticket).
2) Technical deep-dive: Neha will run through a short test plan (we’ll validate keep-alive, connection churn, and streaming tail). Can you confirm two 60–90 min windows next week that work for your infra team?
3) If we see any persistent tail or capacity issues, we’ll present Dedicated sizing and costs as an alternative (likely a committed pool sized for peak concurrency + 20% buffer).

If that sounds reasonable I’ll: (a) ask Sales Ops for the temporary quota increase, (b) send a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive, and (c) draft a pilot MOU (30 days) with success criteria and fallbacks.

Confirm and I’ll get all three started today.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172
